title: Mediating Effects of Essay Writing on the Relationship Between ChatGPT Usage and Critical Thinking in Undergraduate EFL Students: A SmartPLS Approach
venue: International Journal of Pedagogy and Teacher Education
extended_summary:
This paper does not match the requested exact title, "Impact of ChatGPT on the Academic Writing Quality of Senior High School Students." Instead, the provided full text is a different study that examines whether essay-writing skills mediate the relationship between ChatGPT use and critical thinking among undergraduate EFL students. The central question is whether greater ChatGPT use is associated with better essay writing and stronger critical thinking, and whether writing quality serves as a pathway linking AI use to reasoning outcomes.

The study uses a quantitative cross-sectional survey design with PLS-SEM (SmartPLS) and supplementary CFA in AMOS. ChatGPT use was measured through self-reported perceptions such as perceived accuracy, answer satisfaction, usefulness, adaptability, and current information accuracy. Essay writing and critical thinking were also measured through Likert-scale questionnaire items covering thesis clarity, structure, coherence, originality, questioning, inference, evidence evaluation, and related constructs. The approach is correlational rather than experimental: there was no manipulation, no control group, and no direct performance-based writing task scored by raters.

Participants were 201 undergraduate students in the English Education program at Universitas Islam Negeri Sunan Ampel (UINSA) in Surabaya, Indonesia. Data were collected over approximately two months in an EFL higher-education context during regular coursework. The setting appears classroom-based course administration, though the study focuses on survey responses rather than observed instructional implementation.

The main conclusions are that ChatGPT use was positively associated with essay writing (β = 0.613, p < .001) and critical thinking (β = 0.401, p < .001), and that essay writing also positively predicted critical thinking (β = 0.346, p < .001). The indirect effect of ChatGPT on critical thinking through essay writing was significant (β = 0.212, p < .001), indicating partial mediation. The authors argue that guided, writing-centered integration of ChatGPT may support higher-order thinking, but they also caution that measurement issues such as cross-loadings pose threats to discriminant validity and that results should be interpreted carefully.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed correlational cross-sectional survey study using PLS-SEM, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. It has a clear methodology and sample, but relies on self-reported latent constructs without a comparator or causal identification strategy.
impact_tier_rationale: Reported standardized path coefficients are moderate to large (β=0.401 direct to critical thinking; β=0.613 to essay writing; β=0.212 indirect), suggesting substantial positive associations. However, impact should be interpreted cautiously because these are correlational self-report effects rather than intervention effect sizes from a controlled design.

interventions.use_case: Student use of ChatGPT as a conversational AI to support EFL academic essay writing and reasoning, including idea generation, outlining, grammar/style help, research assistance, argument structuring, revision, and feedback during coursework.

ChatGPT used specifically as an AI writing assistant for essay drafting, organization, coherence, grammar/mechanics, citation support, originality awareness, and counterargument development in EFL writing.

finding.finding_summary: In this cross-sectional PLS-SEM study of undergraduate EFL students (N=201), higher reported ChatGPT use was positively associated with essay writing as a latent construct (β=0.613, t=11.799, p<.001). Essay writing was measured through self-reported indicators such as thesis clarity, structure, own reasoning, citations/scholarship, coherence, conciseness, brainstorming, mechanics, originality, and counterargument use; this is not an independently scored posttest of writing products.
finding.measure: Self-reported essay writing latent construct measured by Likert-scale indicators (thesis clarity, topic sentences/structure, own reasoning, citations/scholarship, coherence/flow, conciseness/clarity, brainstorming/introduction, mechanics/citation, originality, counterargument use)

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT use showed a significant positive association with critical thinking among undergraduate EFL students (N=201), with a direct path of β=0.401 (t=5.225, p<.001). Essay writing also positively predicted critical thinking (β=0.346, t=4.445, p<.001), and the indirect effect of ChatGPT on critical thinking through essay writing was significant (β_indirect=0.212, t=4.112, p<.001), indicating partial mediation; all outcomes were self-reported latent constructs rather than independent performance assessments.
finding.measure: Self-reported critical thinking latent construct measured by Likert-scale indicators (questioning, analytical thinking, evidence evaluation, inference, problem solving, creativity, open-mindedness, communication)
finding.effect_size: Direct β=0.401; indirect β=0.212; essay writing→critical thinking β=0.346
finding.std_deviation: Direct STDEV=0.077; indirect STDEV=0.052; essay writing→critical thinking STDEV=0.078
